title: How Enzymes Actually Work
titleOptions: Why Bread Turns Sweet When You Chew It (Enzymes Explained)
Enzymes in 5 Minutes: Active Site, Temperature & pH (GCSE/IGCSE)
hook: Chew a plain cracker for a minute and it starts to taste a little sweet — even though there's almost no sugar in it. The reason is an enzyme in your saliva, doing in seconds what would otherwise take a million years. In this video: what enzymes are, the active site and the lock-and-key model (and why it's a simplification), how temperature and pH affect enzymes, what 'denatured' really means — and two myths that cost marks in exams.
coverage: Covers GCSE (AQA, Edexcel, OCR) and IGCSE (Cambridge 0610, Edexcel 4BI1) enzyme action, temperature and pH. Edexcel and OCR also examine substrate and enzyme concentration, which this video doesn't cover.
